chapters.title: The Orchard Core Title part
chapters.subtitle: Typed titles, generated titles and display text

steps.text: A content item needs a name you can recognize. The Title part gives a content type a title that an editor types, or that the site builds from other fields. Let's add the part, try its behaviors, and generate titles from a pattern.
A content type describes a kind of content, such as a product, and each content item is one entry of that type. A content item can have a display text, which is the name the admin shows in its lists.

An item without a display text is listed under the name of its content type, which makes items of one type hard to tell apart. The Title part gives a content type a title, and stores it as the display text.

An editor can type the title, or the site can generate it from other fields of the item. A Behavior option on the part chooses between four settings: editable, editable and required, generated with the input disabled, or generated with the input hidden.

chapters.title: Add the Title part
chapters.subtitle: Attach it to a content type and open its settings

steps.text: Under Design, Content Definition, Content Types, you find every content type of the site. Product has two Text fields, Brand and Name. Let's click Edit on Product.
Add Parts lists the parts that you can attach to a type. Title is one of them. Add & Configure attaches it and opens its settings.
The settings of the part open. The Behavior option is Title is editable, which is the default. Render Title is checked, so the part renders the title in display views.
Placeholder sets the hint text of an empty Title field. Let's type Product title, and choose Title is editable and required as the Behavior option.
Save stores the settings on the Product type, and a message confirms that the part settings have been saved.
On the Content Types page, Create New Product opens the editor for a product. It has a Title field, and the placeholder text shows in it.
Let's publish with the Title field empty. The title is required, so the item is not saved, and the message reads A value is required for Title.
Let's type Brightwater Camp Stove in the Title field and publish. The item is saved, and the Content Types page opens again.
List Items on the Product row shows its content items. The title you typed is the name of the item in the list.

chapters.title: Generated titles
chapters.subtitle: Build the title from other fields

steps.text: To generate titles, let's edit Product again and then edit the Title part. Let's choose Title is generated and input is disabled as the Behavior option.
The Pattern field appears. It takes a template that can read the fields of the item. Let's combine the Brand field and the Name field, with a space between them.
The editor cannot type in a generated title, so let's clear the Placeholder. Save stores the settings.

On the Content Types page, Create New Product opens the editor with the Title field disabled, and a hint says The title will be auto-generated using the pattern. Let's fill in Brightwater as the Brand and Trail Backpack as the Name, and publish.
List Items shows the item named Brightwater Trail Backpack. The site builds the title again each time the item is saved or published.
Edit opens the item in the editor. The Title field holds the generated title and stays disabled.
Back on the list, View opens the item on the site in a new tab. The heading of the page shows the same title.

chapters.title: Hidden Title field
chapters.subtitle: Generate the title without showing the field

steps.text: The last option hides the field. Let's edit the Title part again, choose Title is generated and input is hidden, and save. The same pattern builds the title.
Back on the Content Types page, Create New Product shows no Title field at all. Let's fill in Brightwater as the Brand and Water Bottle as the Name, and publish.
List Items shows Brightwater Water Bottle. Whichever option you choose, the title ends up as the display text of the content item.
The Title part names your content items: editors type the title, or a pattern generates it, with the field disabled or hidden. Thanks for watching.
